character_facts: The central white-haired woman knows Othon and Aghnar personally and speaks to them in an intimate, emotional farewell.
She cries openly on this page, and another character states this has happened only once before in their experience.
She cannot freely leave because a micro-bomb has been implanted in her chest.
She has superiors above her and considers her actions potentially treasonous to them.
One present character is addressed as 'Mother,' indicating a family relationship within the group.
characters_present: A white-haired woman who is crying and making the confession
A small robot or droid companion
continuity_links: This page appears to occur during a departure or parting scene already in progress.
The dialogue references a prior first occasion when the crying woman was seen crying.
The revelation reframes her earlier refusal to leave as coercion rather than simple choice.
dialogue_meaning: The crying woman tries to leave a vivid memory behind for Othon and Aghnar, linking herself to Okhar's carnivorous flowers.
She refuses to depart with the others, implying a forced separation.
Her tears are presented as rare and significant to those around her.
She admits she concealed the truth deliberately so the others would still leave.
Her final explanation is that she is under lethal control by her superiors through an implanted explosive.

lore_facts: Okhar is associated with carnivorous flowers whose scent is memorable enough to be used as a point of comparison or remembrance.
At least some superiors in this setting enforce loyalty with implanted micro-bombs.
Betrayal in that organization is punished by automatic death rather than ordinary discipline.
Small robot companions exist in this world and can be physically present in intimate personal scenes.
plot_events: A woman emotionally asks Othon and Aghnar not to forget the scent of Okhar's carnivorous flowers.
She states that she cannot accompany the departing group.
One character remarks that this is only the second time they have seen her cry, emphasizing how unusual her emotion is.
Her refusal shocks the others, shown through repeated startled reactions.
She says she withheld the truth until now because telling them earlier might have prevented their departure.
She reveals that a micro-bomb was implanted in her chest.
She explains that her superiors warned her that betraying them would mean death.

visual_summary: A farewell scene turns into a revelation. In cold, metallic surroundings, a white-haired woman embraces or stands close to two white-haired companions while speaking emotionally through tears. Another figure calls attention to her crying, and several shocked close-ups follow. The page then cuts to a large industrial shaft or machinery-filled interior as the woman explains the reason she cannot leave: she says a micro-bomb was implanted in her chest and that her superiors made betrayal a death sentence.
